basic_details.offering_entity: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) & Ministry of Science and ICT, South Korea
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: KAIST Main Campus (Daejeon) and Seoul Campus (College of Business)
basic_details.major_restrictions: Open to all graduate departments in the College of Natural Sciences, College of Life Science & Bioengineering, College of Engineering, and College of Business.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~400 to 500 fully-funded international graduate scholarships awarded annually across Spring and Fall intakes
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open globally; Pakistan is one of the top representation countries at KAIST (~40 to 60 Pakistani scholars selected annually)
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: Master's: 2 years (4 semesters); PhD: 4 years (8 semesters); MS-PhD Integrated: 5 years

nationality_requirements: Non-Korean citizenship (neither applicant nor parents hold Korean nationality; Pakistani citizens eligible)
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: Completed 16 years of education (Bachelor's degree) for Master's; 18 years (Master's degree) for PhD from an accredited university.
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Minimum 3.00 / 4.00 CGPA; competitive admitted candidates typically present 3.50+ / 4.00 CGPA.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Academic background in engineering, computing, natural sciences, or management.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduated or expected to graduate before the semester start date.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Research laboratory experience, programming proficiency, and prior publications in IEEE/ACM/SCI venues significantly boost admission ranking.

english_proficiency.notes: IELTS Academic minimum 6.5, TOEFL iBT minimum 83, or official English Proficiency Certificate (MOI) issued by university registrar.

eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: Korean language (TOPIK) not required; all graduate courses and research conducted in English.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Candidates select 'KAIST Scholarship' on the application portal; no separate scholarship form needed.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Cannot hold another full Korean government scholarship concurrently.

tuition_fee.details: 100% full tuition fee waiver for all regular semesters of study.

admission_application_fee.details: KAIST online application fee (USD $80 / KRW 80,000) paid by applicant.

accommodation.details: Subsidized on-campus university dormitory accommodation provided (~KRW 150,000 to 250,000/month); paid from living stipend.

monthly_stipend.details: KAIST base stipend (KRW 350,000/mo for MS, KRW 400,000/mo for PhD) PLUS research assistantship (RA) top-up from supervising professor lab (~KRW 600,000 to 1,200,000/mo extra). Total take-home typically KRW 1,000,000 to 1,600,000 / month.

airfare.details: Initial airfare to South Korea is paid by student from personal funds or lab advance.

visa_fee.details: Korean student visa (D-2) application fee paid by student at Korean Embassy in Islamabad / Consulate in Karachi.

health_insurance.details: Korean National Health Insurance (NHIS) covered / subsidized by KAIST for international students.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Covered from living allowance and lab resources.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Domestic and international conference travel fully funded through supervisor's research lab grants.

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Single institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST - World Top 55).
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: QS World Rank #53; #1 science and technology university in South Korea.
available_majors: Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence (Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI), Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Robotics, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering, Bio & Brain Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematical Sciences, Industrial & Systems Engineering
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Online application via KAIST admissions portal; select KAIST Scholarship; submit physical or certified digital documents.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: School of Computing and Graduate School of AI are most competitive; contacting professors prior to applying significantly increases chances.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Emailing prospective KAIST lab directors (PIs) with your CV and published work before the deadline to secure informal lab support is strongly advised.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the KAIST application system (Spring intake: August-September; Fall intake: December-January), fill in the online form, pay the $80 application fee, and upload documents.
step_by_step_workflow: 1. Research KAIST laboratories and email prospective professors (November-December for Fall intake).
2. Create account on KAIST International Graduate portal and complete application form.
3. Select 'KAIST Scholarship' as the funding source.
4. Pay the USD $80 online application fee.
5. Designate two academic referees who submit online reference letters.
6. Upload or dispatch required academic certificates, transcripts, and financial sponsor documents before deadline.
7. Departmental committee conducts document screening and video interviews in March.
8. Final admissions and scholarship results announced in late March/early April.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated single application: Select KAIST Scholarship checkbox.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by referees via secure electronic link sent by KAIST.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Statement of Purpose covering academic goals, background, work/research experiences, and future career plans.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Study plan outlining intended research area and courses.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic CV detailing technical skills, publications, and final year projects.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Departmental interview committee or prospective lab PI conducts 20-30 minute video interview in March testing fundamentals and research interest.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: GRE not required; English language score or MOI required.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Apostille or consular legalization by Korean Embassy in Islamabad required for final degree documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Online application followed by document verification.

important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Two annual intakes: Fall intake (Deadline mid-January for Sept start); Spring intake (Deadline late August for March start).

selection_process_and_weights.academic_weight: 40% (Academic record, GPA, mathematical and technical mastery)
selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 35% (Prior lab experience, final year project quality, publications, programming skills)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: KAIST Departmental Admissions Committees and the Central International Admissions Committee.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Two-tier review: Department evaluates academic transcript alignment, lab match, and interview; central committee confirms scholarship.

competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~400 to 500 scholarships awarded annually across both intakes
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~8% to 10% (Strong track record for Pakistani STEM applicants)
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Top engineering and computer science students from leading Pakistani universities with strong programming and research portfolios.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates of NUST, FAST-NUCES, GIKI, UET Lahore, LUMS, Quaid-i-Azam University.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Pakistan, Vietnam, Indonesia, China, Kazakhstan, Turkey, Russia, India.

fake_websites_and_scams: Commercial agents claiming they have 'exclusive quota tie-ups' with KAIST.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Pay only the USD $80 application fee on the official KAIST application portal.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Never work through agents; KAIST requires direct candidate correspondence.
hidden_costs_breakdown: Consular attestation fees at Korean Embassy in Islamabad.
Flight ticket to South Korea (~PKR 180,000 to 250,000).
Initial living expenses for the first month in Daejeon before stipend release.
misleading_claims_debunked: MYTH: You must speak Korean. (Fact: KAIST is an English-medium institution; virtually all graduate classes and research meetings are in English).
MYTH: You cannot apply if you don't have IELTS. (Fact: An official English Proficiency Certificate (MOI) from your Pakistani university is officially accepted).
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: External blogs state the stipend is only KRW 350,000; that is merely the university baseline — active research labs add KRW 600,000 to 1,200,000/mo extra via Research Assistantships (RA).

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 / 4.3 (equivalent to ~2.7/4.0); falling below incurs probation and loss of tuition waiver.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time physical research attendance on campus in Daejeon or Seoul.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Semester credit check and annual research progress evaluation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Part-time work outside the campus requires university and immigration permission under D-2 visa regulations.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None; scholars can seek employment in South Korea's high-tech industry under the D-10 job seeker or E-7 professional work visas.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Expulsion or academic dishonesty results in scholarship revocation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Changing departments requires mutual consent of both department heads.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Tuition waiver is strictly provided for 4 semesters (MS) or 8 semesters (PhD).
